clue.text: Account's given a twist before end of film The Sting

indicators.note: something given a twist is turned round, so the letters of the account abbreviation are read backwards

parts.note: AC is the usual abbreviation for account, and the 's adds an S

indicators.note: the end of the word film supplies just its final letter

explanation.surface: A film reviewer notes the plot twist that comes just before the end of the classic caper movie The Sting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given a twist' turns ACS (AC for account plus the 's) into SCA; the last letter of 'film' completes it. The Sting is the 1973 con-trick film, but here it is just a slang word for a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sting is slang for an elaborate confidence trick, the same as a swindle or con.

clue.text: Sound of insect that's caught fly (tail bitten off)

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its last letter, and here it is bitten off and lost

parts.note: to fly is to rush or hurry

explanation.surface: A cricket that was caught by a predator flew off with its tail bitten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fly' looks like a noun, the insect, but it is the verb meaning to hurry; 'tail bitten off' removes its final Y.
explanation.definitionFit: A churr is the low trilling call of a grasshopper or cricket, also used of some birds.

clue.text: He's driven out of Manchester, possibly, and replaced by one who's a troublemaker?

indicators.note: possibly signals that the remaining letters may be arranged some other way
being driven out of the city name means those letters are removed from it

parts.note: taken as written, the word he, with the 's standing for is
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A man is run out of Manchester and his replacement turns out to be a troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driven out of' removes HE from MANCHESTER, leaving MANCSTER; I for 'one' is added in its place and 'possibly' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: A miscreant is a wrongdoer or villain, someone who causes trouble.

clue.text: This writer, recruited by right-wing president, toed the party line

parts.note: CON is short for Conservative, the right-wing party

indicators.note: being recruited by someone puts one inside their team, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Gerald Ford was a US president
the setter referring to themselves gives ME

explanation.surface: A journalist hired by a right-wing president duly followed the party line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right-wing' gives CON, short for Conservative, and the president is Gerald Ford; 'recruited by' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To conform is to comply with the rules or accepted standards, as a loyal member following the official line does.

clue.text: Talks about husband, popular with various females?

parts.note: C, from Latin circa, is the abbreviation for about
H is the abbreviation for husband in genealogies
something popular is in
WAGs are wives and girlfriends, especially of footballers

explanation.surface: Gossip about a husband who is popular with a number of women.
explanation.walkthrough: WAGs is British tabloid shorthand for the wives and girlfriends of famous footballers.
explanation.definitionFit: A chinwag is an informal chat or gossip, so chinwags are conversations.

clue.text: Canine typically consumes a fair amount

indicators.note: the phrase consumes the letters, holding them within its words

explanation.surface: A dog normally eats a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consumes' signals the run caNINE TYpically.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninety is a substantial number, a fair amount of something.

clue.text: Flipping extracts from Wagnerian operas being broadcast

indicators.note: flipping turns the extracted letters over so they are read from right to left
the letters are extracted from inside the phrase Wagnerian operas

explanation.surface: An exasperated listener complains about bits of Wagner being played on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extracts from' takes RIANO from wagneRIAN Operas, and 'Flipping' turns it round. 'Flipping' looks like a mild British oath.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme on air is going out live on radio or television.

clue.text: Final stages of summertime swell, then very cold conditions, according to this?

definitions.text: Final stages of summertime swell, then very cold conditions, according to this?

indicators.note: the final stages of the word summertime are its closing letters

parts.note: a swell is a dated word for a toff, a posh person
ice forms in very cold conditions

explanation.surface: A forecast warns that summer's last warm spell will give way to a freeze.
explanation.walkthrough: The closing ME of 'summertime' starts it. The Met Office is the UK's national weather service, so the whole clue is the sort of forecast it issues.
explanation.definitionFit: The Meteorological Office issues British weather forecasts, predicting heat and cold alike.

clue.text: As writer, achieve comparatively little during revolution

parts.note: to do something is to achieve it

indicators.note: something happening during an event sits inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a rising is a revolt or revolution
less is the comparative of little

explanation.surface: As an author, a revolutionary feels they are doing little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As writer' hides the definition at the front; 'during' signals the container. Doris Lessing was a British novelist who won the Nobel Prize in 2007.
explanation.definitionFit: Doris Lessing wrote The Golden Notebook and won the Nobel Prize for Literature.

clue.text: Host gathering on Times Square about end of night

indicators.note: about here means round, so the jumbled letters go about another letter
gathering suggests the letters being collected up and rearranged
the end of the word night is its final letter

explanation.surface: A host collects a crowd in Times Square at the end of the night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gathering' rearranges ON TIMES SQUARE and 'about' wraps that round T, the last letter of 'night'.
explanation.definitionFit: A quizmaster presides over a quiz show, acting as its host.

clue.text: Official vehicle parking within northern zone

parts.note: a taxi is a vehicle

indicators.note: within puts the parking letter inside the other pieces

parts.note: a sector is a zone or area
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: An official vehicle is parked in a northern district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'within' puts P inside N plus SECTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tax inspector is a government official who checks returns.

clue.text: Pilots etc boasted at end of show

indicators.note: at the end of tells us the boasting piece comes after the other one

parts.note: to air something is to show it
crew is an old past tense of crow, to boast

explanation.surface: Pilots and others boasted after a display.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boasted' gives CREW, the old past tense of 'crow'.
explanation.definitionFit: The aircrew of a plane are the pilots and other flying staff.

clue.text: Rows about US state taxes

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rows go round the state abbreviation

parts.note: tiffs are quarrels or rows
AR is the postal abbreviation for Arkansas

explanation.surface: Arguments about state taxes in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container; AR is the US postal code for Arkansas, which a non-American solver may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Tariffs are duties levied on imports, a kind of tax.

clue.text: Commanding officer's first to go on Scottish island

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after, so the officer piece follows the island

parts.note: inch is a Scottish word for a small island

indicators.note: the first letter of the officer's word is removed

parts.note: sarge is short for sergeant, an officer, with the 's for has

explanation.surface: An officer is the first to set out for a Scottish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commanding officer' looks like one phrase, but the definition stops at 'Commanding'. 'first to go' drops the S from SARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone in charge is in command, so the phrase means commanding.

clue.text: Dog that ultimately suffered being docked

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: ultimately points to the last letter of the word that

parts.note: to have ailed is to have suffered illness

explanation.surface: A dog that suffered in the end by having its tail docked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' gives T, the last letter of 'that'; 'being' links. Docking a dog means cutting its tail short, which is where the answer's surface joke lies.
explanation.definitionFit: Curtailed means cut short, and docked is used of shortened tails or wages.

clue.text: Case is carried by servant briefly

indicators.note: something carried by another is held inside it
briefly means the word is cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: a valet is a manservant

explanation.surface: A suitcase is carried by a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' docks the servant's last letter, and 'carried by' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: A valise is a small travelling bag or suitcase.

clue.text: A faulty paper with end of page missing is given to a learner as an assessment

indicators.note: faulty means the letters are in the wrong order and must be rearranged
missing means the named letter is taken away
the end of the word page is its last letter

parts.note: L is the learner-driver plate abbreviation

explanation.surface: A poor essay with its last page missing is handed back to a student as a grade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of page missing' removes E from PAPER, leaving PAPR, and 'faulty' rearranges that to PPRA.
explanation.definitionFit: An appraisal is an evaluation, such as a judgment of someone's work.

clue.text: Strikebreaker at centre of riot near American plant

parts.note: a scab is a worker who breaks a strike

indicators.note: the letters at the centre of the word riot are its middle two

explanation.surface: A strikebreaker is caught in the middle of a riot near an American factory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plant' looks like a factory but is a flower. 'at centre of' gives IO, the middle of riot.
explanation.definitionFit: Scabious is a wild flower with pincushion heads, so it is a plant.

clue.text: Goodness gracious, it's hot at the bar

indicators.note: at here places the hot letter beside the bar piece, after it

parts.note: a strut is a bar used as a brace in a framework
H is the abbreviation for hot on taps

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims about the heat in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub, but it is a structural strut. Struth, from God's truth, is an exclamation of surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: Struth is an old exclamation of surprise or dismay, like heavens or blimey.

clue.text: Ruins evening meals, introducing cold starter

indicators.note: introducing means bringing one letter into the other word

parts.note: suppers are evening meals

indicators.note: the starter of the word cold is its first letter

explanation.surface: Bringing a cold starter spoils the dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'starter' looks like a first course but gives C, the first letter of 'cold', and 'introducing' puts it into SUPPERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To scupper a plan is to wreck or ruin it.

clue.text: Shipwreck victim talked of sailors thus

indicators.note: talked of means the words are spoken, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

parts.note: sailors are crews, and thus means so

explanation.surface: A castaway spoke about sailors in this way.
explanation.walkthrough: Robinson Crusoe is the castaway hero of Defoe's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Robinson Crusoe was marooned on an island after a shipwreck in Defoe's story.

clue.text: I'll board transport returning on River Amazon?

indicators.note: returning means the combined letters are turned round and read backwards
to board is to get on, so the letter goes inside the transport word

parts.note: to transport someone is to delight or elate them
taken as I, with the 'll for will

explanation.surface: Someone plans to take a boat back up the Amazon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transport' is a verb, to enrapture. 'board' puts I in ELATE, giving ELIATE, and 'returning' reverses that to ETAILE. Amazon is the online retailer, not the river, with ? marking the example.
explanation.definitionFit: An e-tailer sells online, and the internet shop Amazon is the best-known example.

clue.text: John King, former Wimbledon champ

parts.note: a john is slang for a lavatory, shortened to lav
ER is short for Edward Rex, King Edward

explanation.surface: A list names a king called John alongside an old Wimbledon winner.
explanation.walkthrough: Rod Laver won Wimbledon four times. 'John' looks like a first name but means toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Rod Laver, the Australian tennis player, won several Wimbledon singles titles in the 1960s.

clue.text: Support person, non-U member of caste

parts.note: a bra is a support garment

indicators.note: non-U, read literally, means without the letter U

parts.note: a human is a person

explanation.surface: A supporter of a non-upper-class person who belongs to a caste.
explanation.walkthrough: Non-U is British slang for not upper-class, but here it just says drop U from HUMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Brahmans form the highest, priestly caste in Hindu society.

clue.text: Large house gutted by one New Zealander

indicators.note: gutted means the inside is removed, here the central letter

parts.note: a manor is a large country house
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A mansion is gutted by one Kiwi.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' removes the middle N of MANOR, leaving MAOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the indigenous Polynesian people of New Zealand.

clue.text: Novelist whose works will include one for broadcast on the small screen?

indicators.note: include means the jumbled letters take in one more letter
works suggests the letters being worked into a new arrangement

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: A novelist's books are adapted for television.
explanation.walkthrough: 'works' rearranges NOVELIST WHOSE, and 'include' takes I into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme broadcast on television, the small screen, is a TV programme.

clue.text: Out of condition? Some horses are at end of race

definitions.meaning: a rider is a condition attached to something, and -less means without it

definitions.text: Some horses are at end of race
definitions.meaning: horses that have lost their jockeys finish a race without anyone on board

explanation.surface: Unfit, some horses arrive at the finish of the race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of condition' looks like unfit, but read cryptically it is a word for having no rider, that is no condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is a proviso added to a contract, and horses that unseat their jockeys finish without one on their backs.

clue.text: Place to hide in leafier parts, oddly

indicators.note: the odd-numbered parts of the word leafier, first, third, fifth and seventh

explanation.surface: Something hides in the leafy parts of a wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of leafier.
explanation.definitionFit: A lair is a den where an animal hides.
